route: Work permit (Ministry of Labour and Employment, 'Provision of Work permits')

permit.applies: The engaging company applies to the Ministry of Labour and Employment, with a covering letter from the company and from the worker and a completed application form.
permit.first: An employment contract, copies of the advertisements for the position, and the name and terms of reference of a local counterpart with a training programme.

processing.note: The Ministry states 'about 2-3 weeks' on average.

permit.eligibility: No performer criterion: the Director must certify that no qualified citizen is in the labour market database (s. 163(2)).
permit.feesNote: The Labour Act 2024, Fourth Schedule: a certificate of six months and below M2,000, above six months but below two years M2,500, two years M3,000; the band for the term held is held. The Act has no card fee.

sources.title: Government of Lesotho e-services, Ministry of Labour and Employment: Provision of Work permits
sources.said: Provision of Work permits • Covering letter from the company and personal, • A completed application form • Certified copy of passport including residence permit (where applicable) • Certified copy of educational certificates • Certified copy of a trader`s license certificate (Certified at Trade) • Company income tax clearance certificate • Personal income tax clearance certificate (for renewals) … • Employment Contract copy for professionals • Copies of advertisements for this position • Name and terms of reference of a local counterpart • Organizational structure and a detailed training program … • Application Fee (Non Refundable) … M500.00 • Work-Permits from 6 months and below … M1, 500.00 • Work-Permits above 6 months M2,500.00 • Work-Permits for 2 years M3,000.00 • Printing of Work Permit card M350.00 • Replacement of lost Work Permit … M1,000.00 On average the work permit takes about 2-3 weeks to be issued.

sources.title: Government of Lesotho, 'Lesotho fast-tracks work permits for inbound workers' (LENA, 27 February 2024), quoting the Principal Employment Officer
sources.said: Furthermore, she said applicants will face a fee of M3000.00 for a two-year permit, along with an application fee of M500 plus M350 for a card. The Ministry of Labour and Employment inspect the work permit before the renewal process to see whether one abides by the rules or not. The renewal fee is the same as the initial amount.

sources.title: Lesotho Government Gazette Extraordinary Vol. 69 No. 22, 2 April 2024: Labour Act, 2024 (Act No. 3 of 2024), ss. 1, 161-163 and the Fourth Schedule (an image of the Gazette's own pages, hosted by Laws.Africa)
sources.said: 1. This Act may be cited as the Labour Act, 2024 and shall come into operation on the date of publication in the Gazette. ... 161. (1) No employer shall employ any person in Lesotho who is not a citizen of Lesotho, and no such person shall accept employment in Lesotho, unless that person is in possession of a valid work permit issued by the Director, National Employment Service. ... (4) For purposes of this section, a person who is not a citizen of Lesotho, but who is engaged in Lesotho to provide temporary services shall not be considered to be employed or to have accepted employment ... 163. ... (2) The Director, National Employment Service shall before he grants a non-citizen of Lesotho with a work permit, certify that within the labour market database there is no citizen of Lesotho who qualifies for the available employment. (3) The Minister shall, on the advice of the NACOLA, specify by regulations, the types of work permits, and the duration of validity of each type. ... FOURTH SCHEDULE ... Fees payable 2. (1) An application fee for - (a) a new application, shall be the sum of One Thousand maloti (M1,000.00); and (b) renewal for certificate of employment, shall be the sum of One Thousand Maloti (M1,000.00) and it is non-refundable. (2) The fees payable for a certificate of employment shall be as follows - (a) six months and below, the sum of - M2,000.00 (b) above six months but below two years, the sum of - M2.500.00; and (c) two years, the sum of - M3,000.00

note: An error found and fixed on 2026-11-04: the fees were held from the Ministry's page and its news item (M500 application, M1,500 for six months and below, a M350 card); the Labour Act 2024 (in force 2 April 2024, its Gazette publication read today) sets M1,000 and M2,000 and no card fee, and no regulation made since under s. 163(5) was found, so the Act's figures are held. Its work-permit sections (ss. 161-164 and the Fourth Schedule), read whole, name no union step and no pay rule; a non-citizen engaged to provide temporary services isn't 'employed' (s. 161(4)), with no length stated, so no days are held.
